cf.title: pgstat: Add helper to drop entries from a stats kind's hash

input.subject: [PATCH] pgstat: Add helper to drop entries from a stats kind's hash

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The change adds one argument to an internal function, on master only, and old callers fail at compile time. A committer who knows the area chose the single-function design and reports committing v6 in message #18. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 18 messages and no code were read.

brief.title: Add a stats kind filter to pgstat_drop_matching_entries()
brief.problem: pgstat_drop_matching_entries() scans every variable-numbered stats hash, even when the caller already knows which stats kind it wants. Since 44539786b82 a kind may have its own dshash, so a kind-specific drop does more work than needed. The stated users are extension stats kinds, first pg_stat_statements in follow-up work.
brief.proposed_design: pgstat_drop_matching_entries() gains a stats kind argument. PGSTAT_KIND_INVALID keeps the old all-kinds scan, and a specific kind scans only the hash mapped to that kind. When that hash is the shared variable stats hash, entries of other kinds are skipped before the match callback runs or the NULL-callback drop-all applies.
user_visible_surface: C API: pgstat_drop_matching_entries() takes a new PgStat_Kind argument; existing extension callers must change their call.
C API: PGSTAT_KIND_INVALID passed as kind means all kinds.
Test module test_custom_stats gains SQL test functions for kind-filtered drops.
author_claims: Callers that know their kind avoid scanning unrelated hash tables.
Callers no longer need to repeat the kind check in their match callbacks.
The ABI break is acceptable on master, and updating an extension call is simple.
pg_stat_statements follow-up work will use the kind filter.
brief.thread_state: Bertrand Drouvot and Michael Paquier reviewed it, and the design moved from a separate _of_kind function to one function with a kind argument. Paquier committed a related test fix as 8e225d2ac57d and wrote in message #18 that he committed v6 with two comment tweaks, though the CommitFest entry still says Needs review.
unclear: The material gives no performance numbers for the saved scans.
The thread does not say whether any known extension calls pgstat_drop_matching_entries() today.
The pg_stat_statements follow-up work is not shown, so the actual caller and its match callback are unknown.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: pgstat_drop_matching_entries() in pgstat_internal.h gains a PgStat_Kind argument, so extension callers must change their call.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message says the signature change breaks ABI, so it fits master only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does any known extension call pgstat_drop_matching_entries() today, and should the release notes mention the new argument?
What match callback will the pg_stat_statements follow-up pass, and does it need anything beyond the kind filter?
Is there a measurement of the time saved when a kind with its own dshash skips the shared variable stats hash?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier reviewed the patch, chose the single-function design, and writes in message #18 that he committed v6.
committability.liability: One internal function signature in pgstat_shmem.c and its kind filter on the shared variable stats hash; small, and limited to master.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review within a day and produced six versions; a pg_stat_statements follow-up is announced.

priority.reason: The patch is about 10 KiB, touches one backend file plus a test module, and serves authors of custom stats kinds. Message #18 reports it committed, so the CommitFest entry, still marked Needs review, can be updated.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that the kind filter runs before the match callback and before the NULL-callback drop-all rests on the commit message and message #3. Messages #4 to #18 were not shown in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: WAL-logging facility for pgstats kinds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a new "PgStat" resource manager and a pgstat_xlog_data() entry point so that any pgstats kind, including custom ones, can WAL-log its own stats data. Each kind handles replay through a redo callback in PgStat_KindInfo, so it can decide how the data persists on standbys and after crash recovery.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that stats only make sense on a replica or after a crash when they cover changes that are already WAL-logged, so they should be rebuilt during replay from the WAL records of the underlying objects. For table stats he proposed keying relation stats by relfilenode. He repeated the objection when the entry moved to the next CF, and the author then withdrew the patch and kept it aside.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I can't think of a real case where we would want to WAL log the stats
themselves, rather than re-emitting stats during replay based on the WAL
record of the "underlying object".

precedents_retrieved.title: The Prepare statement with the skewed parameter uses the custom plan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch marks a Const as coming from a Param, and var_eq_const checks whether the column compared to that parameter has skewed statistics. If it does, choose_custom_plan always returns true, so the prepared statement keeps using a custom plan; a later version adds a GUC to control this.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Only the author posted in the thread, and no reviewer replied to the idea or the patches. The entry was withdrawn, and the visible messages do not show a technical objection.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Rename routines for write/read of pgstats file"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Rename routines for write/read of pgstats file"
Reverted commit(s): Rename routines for write/read of pgstats file
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit ed823da1289, that has made pgstat_write_chunk() and
pgstat_read_chunk() available for public use.  These routines do not
have a symmetric API definition across reads and writes, with the write
part returning a void status, deferring an error detection once all the
stats entries have been processed with an ferror(), and the read part
returning a boolean status.

These routines are just tiny wrappers around fread() and fwrite(), and
extensions can just define they own routines instead of relying on the
same facilities as the core pgstat.c.  This commit removes their
declaration from the public headers, to reduce the confusion.
test_custom_stats is updated to use its own read/write routines.
Perhaps something better could be designed in the future; trying to do
so for v19 is not feasable during beta.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move all am-related reloption code into src/backend/access/[am-name] and get rid of relopt_kind for custom AM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves reloption definitions out of reloptions.c into per-access-method option lists returned by a new amrelopt_catalog AM function, replaces amoptions, and puts generic option parsing into a new options.c. It also replaces StdRdOptions with per-relation-type structures, renames the Relation* macros, adds an enum option type, and rejects toast options on tables without a TOAST table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked that the patch be split, because the new tests and the TOAST table checks belonged in separate patches. Michael Paquier objected that the patch gives extensions no equivalent of add_int_reloption() and add_real_reloption(), and that the macro renames and other diff noise break APIs. The author did not post an update for two weeks, and then agreed to split the work into smaller patches.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is still no API equivalent for add_int_reloption(),
add_real_reloption(), which is a problem as extension should be
allowed to still use that.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PG19]pg_dump --statistics restores extended statistics by attribute number
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_dump --statistics writes extended statistics (ndistinct, dependencies) with the source table's attribute numbers, which can be invalid or point to other columns after restore. The patch passed source column numbers and names to pg_restore_extended_stats and remapped them by name; v2 only rejected the data when the column names did not match.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier said name-based mapping has its own problems, such as a column renamed to a former column's name, and that the logical vs physical attnum issue is old and not worth dozens of hours. Corey Huinker said the restored stats are overwritten by the next autovacuum and that rejected stats are caught by vacuumdb --missing-stats-only. On v2, Michael Paquier doubted the inheritance-child case happens in practice and saw nothing worth acting on, so the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I mean that there is nothing that I see worth acting on here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow index AMs to calculate custom statistics / BRIN
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets index AMs compute their own statistics during ANALYZE through a new opclass support procedure and store them in a new bytea column, staindexam, in pg_statistic. For BRIN minmax it computes the average number of overlapping ranges, matching ranges per value, and null and summarization counts, and brincostestimate() uses the overlap count, behind a new GUC enable_indexam_stats.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No design objection appears in the visible messages. The CF entry failed tests from submission, and Andres Freund asked whether the author planned further work, proposing to close the entry otherwise. No reply from the author is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This CF entry has been failing tests since it was submitted. Are you planning
to work on this further?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: add the last checkpoint kind to the control file
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Julien Rouhaud, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: Store the flags of the last completed checkpoint (shutdown, end-of-recovery, immediate, force and so on) in the control file. Show them through pg_control_checkpoint() and pg_controldata, so users can see the checkpoint kind without reading the server logs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers saw no realistic use for the kind of an already completed checkpoint and preferred a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view for the checkpoint in progress. The control file must stay within 512 bytes, so its space is kept for critical data, and two bytes for non-critical data were judged a likely future regret. The stored flags also leave out flags added when a running checkpoint is upgraded, for example by a later CHECKPOINT command. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For now we have some room, but we will likely keep consuming bytes in that file
for more critical features and it's almost certain that at one point we will
regret wasting 2 bytes for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pluggable toaster
precedents_retrieved.authors: Fedor Sigaev (sigaev), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Oleg Bartunov (oleg), Nikita Malakhov (nmalakh)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Matthias van de Meent, Aleksander Alekseev
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds a toaster API, like the table AM API, so extensions can plug in custom toasters per column, with new SQL syntax and a custom toast pointer format, and routes the built-in toaster through it. Later revisions moved toaster assignments into a new catalog pg_toastrel, added DROP TOASTER, and planned a hooks-based extension version.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the patches add a lot of code and complexity without fixing any TOAST problem, and said he would not accept the planned hooks either. Matthias van de Meent and Aleksander Alekseev said a complex design was posted before there was community agreement on how type-aware TOAST should work, and asked for that design discussion first. Aleksander Alekseev also cited maintenance cost and benchmarks that others could not reproduce, and moved the discussion to the compression dictionaries thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The problem for me is that what you've been posting doesn't actually fix any problem, but instead introduces lots of new code and complexity.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add option --drop-cascade for pg_dump/restore
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a --drop-cascade option to pg_dump and pg_restore that adds CASCADE to each DROP command emitted under --clean. It reuses the code path that --if-exists uses to edit DROP statements, so an old dump can be restored over a database that has gained new dependent constraints.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. After Tom Lane said in November 2021 that the patch needed another rebase, and recommended moving the DROP-editing SQL code out of RestoreArchive into its own function, no new version came. Daniel Gustafsson then marked the entry Returned with Feedback. Earlier, Tom Lane called editing DROP commands in pg_restore fragile; the author replied that --if-exists already does this.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As this patch hasn't been updated, I'm marking this entry Returned with
Feedback.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at this idea, and the thread points to no earlier proposal. The only earlier work the thread names is 44539786b82, which this patch builds on, and the lost injection_points test (message #9, #11), which was restored as 8e225d2ac57d.

From the standards and compatibility angle, there is nothing to object to. The change has no SQL syntax, GUC, pg_dump, psql or client-visible effect. The only contract change is the signature of pgstat_drop_matching_entries() in pgstat_internal.h, on master only, and old callers fail at compile time rather than misbehaving at run time. The use of PGSTAT_KIND_INVALID to mean all kinds was raised in message #9 and settled in message #11. Message #18 reports the patch as committed.

The proposal changes no persistent or cross-node state: no stats file format, WAL record, catalog, or wire protocol change, and it only narrows which shared-memory dshash an in-memory drop scans. The signature change to pgstat_drop_matching_entries() in pgstat_internal.h targets master only, and old callers fail at compile time, so the break is visible to extension authors.

The proposal changes an internal C function in pgstat_internal.h that only server code and loaded extensions can call. It adds no SQL-callable surface outside the test module and no new privilege, view or GUC. It does not change what any role can see or do. The kind filter only narrows which entries a drop can touch, so it lowers the chance of dropping other kinds' entries. Exposure is unchanged.

From the maintenance angle there is no objection a committer would send. The change only adds a kind argument to an existing internal function, so the hot path is untouched and no per-kind registration point is added. The area committer reviewed the change, chose the single-function design in message #4, and reports committing v6 in message #18. Two points cannot be checked from the material: no numbers show the saving from the skipped scans, and the pg_stat_statements caller is not shown. Neither one supports a concrete failure scenario.

The existing idiom is pgstat_drop_matching_entries() with a callback that checks entry->key.kind, as the old injection_points test did. That idiom still scans every variable-numbered hash, including the shared hash with all relation entries, and no extension or hook can avoid that scan outside pgstat_shmem.c. The patch extends the existing function rather than adding a second mechanism, so this angle has no objection. The thread shows no performance numbers, and the brief already notes that.

Demand is modest but real. The removed injection_points test filtered by kind in its callback (message #11), and pg_stat_statements is the named next caller. The cost is one internal signature change on master, borne by the few kind-aware extensions, and the area committer reviewed and committed it (message #18).
